body: The spec's data foundation is unverifiable and internally inconsistent, which matters because every downstream requirement depends on it. (1) The idea document cites OpenML dataset ID 42123; the spec's FR-001 cites ID 2352 — one of these is wrong, and neither is established to actually be a 'Surface Roughness & Tribology' dataset containing roughness descriptors and both target variables; FR-012 checks for target columns but nothing establishes the dataset exists at all. (2) The NIST DOI is literally blank in FR-001, FR-003, and the Assumptions ('DOI )'), so the second data source is a placeholder, not a commitment. (3) FR-004 changes the outlier rule from the idea's ±3σ to a MAD rule without noting the change — defensible, but the cross-reference error in the Assumptions ('imputed using median imputation as described in FR-004') points at the outlier-removal requirement, not an imputation requirement; there is no FR defining median imputation at all. (4) FR-016's fallback validation is statistically incoherent: a Kolmogorov-Smirnov test on marginal distributions of roughness columns cannot establish that fallback columns are 'statistically comparable' to pySurf-derived descriptors computed from raw profilometry — these are different quantities on different supports, and p > 0.05 only fails to reject, it does not confirm equivalence. (5) FR-013 is missing from the numbering. Finally, FR-011/US-3 scenario 3 hard-codes physical priors (e.g., hardness inversely correlates with wear) as validation criteria — but the research question asks which parameters predict tribological outcomes, so using assumed answers to validate the model risks confirming the priors rather than testing them.
